examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Convergence of a Geometric Series With an Arbitrary Starting Index
examples.problem:
Determine whether the following geometric series converges or diverges.

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty {3}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{n}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
The series starts with $n=0.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{0}} & =\frac{3{(\frac{3}{2})}^{1}}{3{(\frac{3}{2})}^{0}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r| \geq 1.$

feedback.problem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{6}{(-1)}^{n}$ ?
feedback.worked_solution:
The series starts with $n=1.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{\frac{1}{6}{(-1)}^{2}}{\frac{1}{6}{(-1)}^{1}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r|\ge 1.$
